proposed.explanation:
COMI (Commercial International Bank of Egypt) shows strong fundamental growth in FY2025 versus FY2024: net loans grew ~48% (from 343.5 bn to 508.0 bn EGP), customer deposits grew ~14% (from 972.6 bn to 1,110.4 bn EGP), net interest income grew ~18% (from 91.1 bn to 107.7 bn EGP), and basic EPS rose ~24% (from 14.72 to 18.25 EGP per share). At the current price of 128 EGP, the implied P/E is roughly 7×, which is low for a bank posting this rate of earnings growth and suggests the market may be underpricing the stock's trajectory.

For your profile—10-year horizon, high-growth objective, high loss tolerance, no liquidity needs—this is a reasonable entry. The bank is expanding its loan book aggressively, which is the primary engine of a bank's earnings, and the deposit base is growing to support that expansion. A ~7× P/E on 24% EPS growth offers an attractive growth-to-valuation ratio.

I recommend buying 58 shares (cost: 7,424 EGP), which is the maximum allowed under the diversification rule (no single holding may exceed 50% of total portfolio value). After the purchase you would hold 7,424 EGP in COMI and 7,576 EGP in cash, for a total portfolio of 15,000 EGP, with COMI at 49.5% of the portfolio.

Risks and limitations: (1) We have only one year of comparative data; a single-year spike in loan growth (48%) may partly reflect EGP inflation rather than real credit expansion. (2) No information on non-performing loan ratios, capital adequacy, or provisioning is available, so credit-quality risk is unassessed. (3) The low P/E could reflect genuine market concerns about the Egyptian banking sector that are not visible in this evidence. (4) You would be concentrating nearly half your portfolio in a single stock; the remaining cash should be deployed into other names over time to build diversification. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
